topic: Garp trained Luffy's body years before Rayleigh taught him Haki
title: Garp Trained Luffy Before Rayleigh Did
description: Garp raised Luffy long before Silvers Rayleigh taught him Haki. Who taught Haki in One Piece is a bigger chain than most fans think, and the full breakdown is linked above.
comment: Did Garp's physical training matter more than Rayleigh's Haki lessons, or the other way round?

lines.text: Everyone says Rayleigh taught Luffy Haki. But Garp had him for years first.

shot.fallback: anime style, marine grandfather standing over a small boy

lines.text: Garp raised Luffy in Foosha Village with brutal physical training.

shot.search: Monkey D. Garp Luffy Foosha Village
shot.fallback: anime style, old marine and young boy on a village path

lines.text: Sources describe him tying Luffy to a balloon and dropping him from heights.

shot.fallback: anime style, small boy tied to a floating balloon over the sea

lines.text: None of the sources I checked credit Garp with teaching Haki in those years.

shot.fallback: anime style, marine captain staring into the distance

lines.text: So Garp built the body, and Haki came later from a different teacher.

shot.fallback: anime style, boy bouncing back up after a hard fall

lines.text: Rayleigh then spent about two years on Rusukaina teaching all three types.

shot.fallback: anime style, mentor with a wide hat on a wild island

lines.text: Here's my read: Garp's toughness is why Luffy could survive that training at all.

shot.fallback: anime style, pirate standing firm under a waterfall

lines.text: That's a theory, not canon, so tell me which teacher you'd pick.

shot.fallback: anime style, old marine with a proud expression

lines.text: But if Garp never taught Haki, what did he teach Luffy that Rayleigh never could?

shot.fallback: anime style, marine leader looking down at a boy

self_check.hook: Line 1 names Garp and Luffy and the Haki claim in under 2 seconds.
self_check.loop: The last line asks what Garp taught that Rayleigh never could, which leads back into the opening contrast.
